hypotheses.text: Epilepsy in NKX6-2-related disorder does not selectively segregate with diffuse cerebral hypomyelination on neuroimaging, but occurs as an independent manifestation observable both in patients lacking overt hypomyelination and absent in patients with severe diffuse hypomyelination.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolves the direct contradiction identified in deep testing regarding the proposed clustering of epilepsy with diffuse hypomyelination. Clarifying whether epilepsy is truly dissociated from white matter hypomyelination status is essential for accurate clinical stratification.

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2020) demonstrated in an expanded cohort of 11 new cases from 8 families alongside literature cases that phenotypes with epilepsy in the absence of overt hypomyelination occur, as well as diffuse hypomyelination without seizures.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: The phenotypic and neuroimaging expression in NKX6-2 is described and it is shown that phenotypes with epilepsy in the absence of overt hypomyelination and diffuse hypomyelination without seizures can occur.

hypotheses.text: Nystagmus (HP:0000639) is a core neuro-ophthalmological feature shared across both mild (childhood-onset) and severe (infantile/neonatal-onset) NKX6-2 disease spectra, rather than being an exclusive marker of diffuse hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
hypotheses.rationale: The original binned hypothesis asserted that early nystagmus selectively clusters with diffuse hypomyelination, but clinical descriptions suggest nystagmus manifests across the spectrum as part of the cerebellar ataxia presentation regardless of hypomyelination severity.

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2018 GeneReviews) note that nystagmus is documented across both the severe end (neonatal-onset nystagmus) and the milder end of the spectrum (complex spastic ataxia with cerebellar findings including nystagmus, extraocular movement disorder, dysarthria, titubation, and ataxia).

source.title: NKX6-2-related disorder
source.quote: At the milder end of the spectrum is normal achievement of early motor milestones in the first year of life followed by slowly progressive complex spastic ataxia with pyramidal findings... and cerebellar findings (nystagmus, extraocular movement disorder, dysarthria, titubation, and ataxia)

numbers.metric: total reported individuals reviewed in GeneReviews

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2020) emphasize that NKX6-2 mutations should be suspected specifically when very early onset nystagmus, cerebellar ataxia, and hypotonia progressing to spasticity occur, particularly when neuroimaging signs of hypomyelination are present.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: NKX6-2 mutations should be considered in patients with autosomal recessive, very early onset of nystagmus, cerebellar ataxia with hypotonia that rapidly progresses to spasticity, particularly when associated with neuroimaging signs of hypomyelination.

hypotheses.text: Global psychomotor developmental delay (HP:0001263) segregates with age of onset and overall functional severity in NKX6-2-related disease, presenting predominantly in neonatal- and infantile-onset cases rather than serving as an invariant obligate finding in childhood-onset spastic ataxia.
hypotheses.rationale: Contrasts the invariant findings (spasticity and cerebellar ataxia) against global psychomotor delay, testing whether developmental delay is restricted to the severe infantile spectrum or universal.

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2020) demonstrated a bifurcated clinical spectrum characterized by neonatal onset with global psychomotor delay and worse prognosis at the severe end, contrasting with childhood onset with a mainly motor spastic ataxia phenotype at the milder end.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: Our data reveal a phenotype spectrum with neonatal onset, global psychomotor delay and worse prognosis at the severe end and a childhood onset with mainly motor phenotype at the milder end.

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2017) observed individuals from two families with childhood-onset disease and very slow progression who survived into their 30s and 40s presenting with predominant ataxia and cerebellar atrophy rather than early devastating global psychomotor arrest.

source.title: Mutations in NKX6-2 Cause Progressive Spastic Ataxia and Hypomyelination
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Affected members of two families had childhood onset disease with very slow progression. They are still alive in their 30s and 40s and show predominant ataxia and cerebellar atrophy features on imaging.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance and semiology of epileptic seizures in SPAX8 patients with isolated cerebellar atrophy versus those with diffuse hypomyelination?
new_directions.rationale: Since Chelban et al. (2020) confirmed seizures occur without hypomyelination, establishing precise prevalence rates and seizure types across MRI subtypes will define whether epilepsy is a primary cortical/subcortical network defect of NKX6-2 deficiency.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of neonatal hypotonia that transitions to spasticity discriminate severe infantile SPAX8 from classical Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease and GJC2/PMLD1?
new_directions.rationale: Chelban et al. (2020) highlight hypotonia rapidly progressing to spasticity as a hallmark presentation of severe NKX6-2 disorder; determining if this specific dynamic trajectory is distinguishing would aid differential diagnosis.
